content: Teddy Grahams are small, bear-shaped graham cracker snacks that were first introduced by Nabisco in 1988. Over the years, they have been released in various forms, including a cereal version and a short-lived product called Dizzy Grizzlies. However, the core flavors of Teddy Grahams have consistently included cinnamon, honey, and chocolate. More recently, additional flavors such as chocolate chip and oatmeal have been introduced. The snacks have retained their iconic bear shapes, which include bears with arms raised and legs closed, as well as bears with legs open and arms lowered. Teddy Grahams have occasionally been featured in popular culture. They were used as a prop on Late Night with Conan O'Brien, referenced in an episode of The Simpsons, and mentioned in a Strong Bad email. Additionally, the snack was referenced in the song Ridin' Rims by Dem Franchize Boys. Nutritional Information Nabisco has marketed Teddy Grahams as a healthy snack option. However, this claim has faced criticism. A New York Times article by Marian Burros highlighted that the snacks contained more bleached flour than whole wheat graham flour. In response to this criticism, Nabisco increased the amount of whole grain flour used in the product. Teddy Grahams are free of trans fats and are considered a good source of calcium and iron. Furthermore, according to PETA, the chocolate and cinnamon varieties of Teddy Grahams are vegan-friendly. Advertising In recent years, advertisements for Teddy Grahams have become rare. The most recent ad appeared on PBS and featured a toddler eating Teddy Grahams while running around his house. Historically, Teddy Grahams commercials included catchy jingles and featured animated bear characters. For example, one jingle celebrated the scrumptious bunch of bite-sized bears available in honey, cinnamon, and chocolate flavors. Another jingle introduced Teddy Grahams Breakfast Bears cereal, emphasizing its wholesome graham goodness and its role as part of a nutritious breakfast. A later campaign introduced Teddy Grahams Rockin’ Bears, which featured new shapes and flavors like vanilla and chocolate, accompanied by a rock music theme. These commercials often highlighted the fun and delicious nature of the snack.
